page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. This CPU features 40 physical cores and 40 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 4.8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying on external storage solutions. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The processor achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07, supported by hardware-level instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. Memory performance tests show a cached read-only bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a write bandwidth of 48.09 GB/sec. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 25.35 GB/sec and processed 34.78 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. For language model inference, the system processed 1841.39 tokens per second on a small 135M model, but throughput decreased to 56.94 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model.

The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators represents a key architectural tradeoff, limiting this instance's utility for direct high-speed local database logging or heavy parallel graphics processing. However, the dedicated physical core allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio make it suitable for compute-intensive tasks that require consistent CPU performance without hyperthreading interference. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, text and image processing, web serving, and medium-scale database operations that utilize network-attached storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a dedicated x86_64 server instance featuring 40 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at 3.1 GHz with 192.0 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, the instance relies on network-attached storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 38378.07 and a Passmark CPU score of 34691.95. It supports AVX-512 vector instructions, enabling efficient execution of cryptographic and vector-based operations. The instance is suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and database operations that benefit from dedicated physical cores and a balanced memory-to-CPU ratio without hyperthreading overhead.
